changes.comment: Panes and tabs: the editor area is now a split tree of panes, each with its own tab strip, its own status bar and its own note. Alt+- and Alt+= split, Ctrl+Mod+Arrows move between panes, Ctrl+Mod+Backspace closes one and Ctrl+Mod+- closes a pane's other tabs.

Every open is a tab (Mod+T, Mod+W, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Mod+Shift+T). A note already open in that pane is activated rather than opened twice; Mod+click in the tree or the links panel, and Mod+Enter in quick-open, open in the background.

A tab remembers where you were: switching away and back lands the caret and the scroll where they were, and undo survives the switch because the undo stack belongs to the note rather than to the view.
Only the note on screen in each pane holds an editor, so leaving twenty tabs open costs a path and a cursor each — memory follows the number of panes, never the number of tabs.

Drag builds the layout: drag a tab onto another pane's strip to move it, onto a pane's middle to join it, or onto one of its edges to split there. Every one of those has a menu equivalent in the tab's right-click menu.

Every split border is a drag handle and a keyboard separator (Tab to it, then arrows), and the sizes are remembered per vault on this device — as is the whole layout, restored at the next start and checked against the vault first.

A pane mode, Zellij-style: Mod+P then single letters — n d r x f p w to make and move panes, h j k l (or the arrows) to move between them, and m / s / t sub-modes for moving, resizing and tabs. A bar along the bottom shows what every key does while the mode is live.
Zoom (Mod+P then f) gives one pane the whole editor area and puts the rest away without taking them apart; the pane's status bar says it is zoomed.
Back and forward (Mod+[ / Mod+]) now walk the tab's own trail rather than one list for the whole window, so they never jump you to another pane.
Each pane's sync pill is its own note's: two panes on one note read the same record, so they can never disagree.
An empty tab offers the vault: type to filter, Enter to open it in that tab.
Deleting or renaming a note now follows every tab that holds it, in every pane, and a note that no longer exists never comes back at the next start.
Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab now match on Linux and Windows: a Ctrl-only shortcut used to be unreachable there.
